title: Credit-aware source sync
description: Stop syncs that cannot pay for themselves, and turn credit exhaustion into a typed, resumable outcome that clients can act on.

stories.title: Refuse to start a sync for a registered user with no usable credits
stories.description: Check the caller's credit balance before a sync job is created or enqueued, and return a stable machine-readable refusal instead of letting the job fail later.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a sync as a registered user with zero usable credits fails with a typed credit-required response instead of a started job.
No sync job row is written and no queue message is published when the request is refused.
No provider request is made when the request is refused.
The refusal carries a stable reason code and the caller's available credit count, and contains no operation name, class name, or nested cause.
All three sync entry points enforce the rule: starting a sync, replaying a sync, and creating a source with sync requested.
Anonymous and x402-paid source flows keep working unchanged and are never refused for lack of credits.
A user with at least one usable credit can still start a sync.
implementation_notes: The billing repository already exposes a method that returns a user's available credit total; reuse it rather than querying the ledger again.
The credit-required reason code introduced here is the shared vocabulary for the rest of this epic. Define it once in a place both the start boundary and the job outcome can import.
Source creation starts a sync when the caller is anonymous or when the request asks for it. Only the registered-user branch is billable.
Registered users whose source was claimed through an x402 payment do not spend credits on records retained at claim time; do not refuse those callers on balance alone.
testing_notes: Drive the tests through the authenticated HTTP API, not the service layer, so the rule is proven for SDK and CLI callers too.
Assert the absence of side effects explicitly: no persisted job, no enqueued message, no provider call.
Cover the zero-credit refusal and the one-credit success on the same entry point so the boundary is exact.

stories.title: Separate fetched provider records from persisted transactions in sync progress
stories.description: The progress counter labelled Imported counts raw provider records that were fetched and cached, which reads as usable imported transactions. Make the public meaning unambiguous.
acceptance_criteria: The counter that measures fetched provider records is named and labelled so it cannot be read as persisted transactions.
A failed sync that fetched many provider records and persisted none does not display a large Imported total.
The job status response, the SDK type, and the web progress display all use the clarified naming.
A test asserts the counter's meaning against a run where fetched and persisted counts differ.
implementation_notes: The counter is incremented by the size of each fetched provider batch during the discovery loop, before normalization runs, so it has always measured cached provider records.
The product is pre-launch, so rename the public field rather than adding a parallel one; do not keep a compatibility alias.
This story is independent of the credit work and can land alongside SYNC-001.
testing_notes: Prove the distinction with a case where records are fetched but zero transactions are persisted; equal counts would hide a wrong label.
Include the web progress display in the assertions, since the label is what the user actually reads.

stories.title: Report mid-sync credit exhaustion as a typed resumable outcome
stories.description: Promote credit exhaustion from a generic storage failure to a domain outcome that reaches clients as a stable reason code with credit counts, and keep the internal cause in logs only.
acceptance_criteria: A sync that starts with fewer credits than it needs keeps the covered transactions committed and ends in a credit-required state, not a generic failure.
The job status response exposes the credit-required reason code, the credits available, the credits consumed, and the additional credits required once the billable total is known.
The job status response contains no persistence operation name, internal class name, nested cause, or SQL detail in any field.
The credit-required state is marked resumable, distinct from a terminal failure.
Structured logs still record the internal cause together with the source and job identifiers.
One place maps internal sync outcomes to public reason codes and allowed actions; handlers and clients do not each interpret raw errors.
implementation_notes: Credit exhaustion is currently raised as a storage error carrying a dedicated operation string, then wrapped again by normalization and stored whole in the job record.
Reuse the reason code introduced in SYNC-001 so the pre-flight refusal and the mid-sync outcome speak the same vocabulary.
The additional-credits figure is only knowable once the billable total is counted; report it when known rather than guessing early.
The BullMQ consumer already treats credit exhaustion as terminal for retry purposes; keep that behavior while changing how the outcome is reported.
testing_notes: Set up a source with more new billable transactions than the available balance, so the run is partly paid for.
Assert the committed transactions survive and their credits stay consumed.
Assert on the shape of the public response, including a negative assertion that no field leaks internal identifiers.
Cover the worker-to-API path, not just the persistence boundary, since that is where the wrapping happened.

stories.title: Prove that continuing after buying credits reuses cached work
stories.description: Add the missing coverage for resuming a credit-paused sync, and close any gap it exposes, so a purchase does not refetch provider history or pay twice for a transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Continuing a credit-paused sync after credits are added completes the remaining transactions.
Provider history already fetched before the pause is not requested again.
Transactions charged before the pause are not charged a second time, and the final ledger balance matches one charge per billable transaction.
Continuing twice in a row produces the same result as continuing once.
The continue path is reachable through the public API, not only from an internal service.
implementation_notes: Credit consumption already keys on a stable per-transaction reference and looks up prior charges by both raw record and external id, so double-charging is probably already prevented. Confirm with a test before writing new guard code.
Sync execution already carries checkpoint and high-watermark resume state, so the reuse of cached history may need no new machinery either.
If both hold, this story is mostly the missing test plus whatever public action exposes continuation. Do not add a second credit-reservation mechanism.
testing_notes: Write this as an integration test against a real database so the ledger arithmetic is genuinely checked.
Count provider calls across the pause to prove history is not refetched.
Run the continue action twice to prove it is idempotent.

stories.title: Show a billing action instead of Retry when a sync runs out of credits
stories.description: Render the sync island's credit-required state from the typed API fields, with safe copy and the billing action that matches the user's subscription, and no generic Retry.
acceptance_criteria: A credit-required sync shows copy explaining what happened and what is needed, with no operation name, class name, or nested cause on screen.
A credit-required sync offers no Retry action.
A user without an active subscription is offered the choose-a-plan action.
A subscriber whose credits are exhausted is offered the credit-purchase action.
Other failures keep their existing Retry behavior.
The copy comes from the response's reason code and credit fields, not from parsing the message text.
implementation_notes: The island currently renders any failed job with the raw message plus an unconditional Retry button.

The billing status endpoint already returns credits, subscription status, and period end, and the billing route already distinguishes an active subscriber from an unsubscribed user; reuse that logic instead of writing a second version.
Keep this story inside the sync island's failed state. Pre-sync gating, first-run onboarding, and dashboard empty states belong to issue #108.
testing_notes: Cover both billing states with the same credit-required outcome, since the reason code is identical and only the offered action differs.
Assert the absence of the Retry control for credit-required outcomes and its presence for an unrelated failure.
Assert that internal identifiers from a nested cause never reach the rendered output.
